form.official-title: To require the Securities and Exchange Commission, when developing rules and regulations about disclosures to retail investors, to conduct investor testing, including a survey and interviews of retail investors, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the SEC Disclosure Effectiveness Testing Act.

subsection.text: Section 23(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (15 U.S.C. 78w(a)) is amended by adding at the end the following:

subparagraph.text: The Commission shall engage in investor testing prior to issuing any rule or regulation which designates documents or information to be disclosed under the securities laws, if such documents or information—

clause.text: are primarily used by retail investors, as determined by the Commission; and
are intended to be used by retail investors to make informed investment decisions or to understand the investments held by the retail investor.

subparagraph.text: Investor testing conducted pursuant to subparagraph (A) shall include the following:

clause.text: Qualitative testing in the form of one-on-one cognitive interviews of retail investors about documents or information, or samples of such documents or information, to be provided.
A nationwide survey of retail investors, designed to complement the interviews under clause (i), on—

subclause.text: the usefulness of such documents or information, or samples of such documents or information;
the proposed format of such documents or information, or samples of such documents or information; and
delivery preferences of such documents or information, or samples of such documents or information.

clause.text: Analysis and publication in the Federal Register of the results of the survey and interviews.
An opportunity for the public to comment on such results published in the Federal Register.

subparagraph.text: If the Commission, in the period between engaging in investor testing and publishing a final rule, makes substantive changes to such rule that the Commission determines would have a significant impact on retail investors, the Commission shall again engage in investor testing.

subparagraph.header: Public availability of retail testing results
subparagraph.text: The Commission shall make the data and results of any investor testing performed pursuant to this paragraph available to the public.

subsection.text: Section 4(g) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (15 U.S.C. 78d(g)) is amended—

subparagraph.text: in subparagraph (D)(ii), by striking and at the end;
by redesignating subparagraph (E) as subparagraph (F); and
by inserting after subparagraph (D) the following:

clause.text: as necessary to carry out the functions of the Office; and
under section 23(a)(4), if the Commission determines it appropriate; and

paragraph.text: by adding at the end the following:

paragraph.header: Publication of data and results of investor testing
paragraph.text: With respect to any investor testing carried out by the Investor Advocate pursuant to paragraph (4)(E), the Investor Advocate may make the data and results of such investor testing available to the public, and without further review or editing by the Commission.

For any final rule or regulation issued by the Securities and Exchange Commission (in this subsection referred to as the Commission) before the date of the enactment of this Act that would be subject to investor testing under section 23(a)(4) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, had such rule been issued on or after the date of enactment of this Act, the Commission shall perform investor testing with respect to such rule or regulation that includes the contents described in such section 23(a)(4).

The Commission shall, not later than 6 months after the date of the enactment of this Act, establish a schedule for completing any investor testing required under paragraph (1) that prioritizes testing of any final rules and regulations that designate documents or information central to retail investor decision making.
The Commission shall issue a report to Congress each year containing the following:

subparagraph.text: The status of any investor testing required under paragraph (1).
The results of any investor testing completed under paragraph (1).
Any priorities the Commission has, based on results of investor testing required by paragraph (1), for—

clause.text: revising or eliminating any final rule or regulation designating documents or information to be provided to retail investors; and
revising any other final rule or regulation to supplement revised or eliminated rules designating documents or information to be provided to retail investors.
